_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: An MCP tool's view renders and works with the conversation. The MCP server "counter" has the tool show_counter, whose view shows a counter, the app-only tool increment, and the tool leave, whose view goes to another page before it loads. The agent has run, in the conversation /c/{{SLUG}}, "shelley mcp call counter.show_counter start=1" and then "shelley mcp call counter.leave". Each call's view shows in the conversation in a card (data-testid "message-mcpapp") as an iframe titled with the call's name: "the view" is the frame "iframe[title='counter.show_counter']", and "the left view" the frame "iframe[title='counter.leave']". The view's elements are #count, #input, #theme, #background, #mode, #connect, #eval, #worker and #worker-connect, and the buttons #increment, #tell (asks the host to send "echo: counter at" and the count as the user's message, then shows in #told how that went: "sent" or "declined", and how many times it has heard back, or the error), #keep (does what #tell does, but keeps the focus from moving to it, as canvases and toolbars do), #fullscreen and #leave; its scripts define window.tell(text) (asks the host to send text as the user's message), window.fullscreen() (asks the host for fullscreen and returns the mode it got), window.grab() (takes the focus, if it can, for #tell, and says whether it has it), window.handOn() (hands every port the view holds to another one) and window.overheard (what reached the ports handed on). The page a view goes to has #sent. "The card" is the data-testid "message-mcpapp" whose text contains "counter.show_counter", and "the frame" its data-testid "mcp-app-frame". Call "agent told" says whether the agent was told the user sees the result in an interactive view ("true" or "false"). Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does; "named X" means an exact name match. "The consent bar" is data-testid "mcp-app-consent", where the host asks the user's OK for links and downloads a view asks for. "The text box" is data-testid "message-input", and "the draft label" data-testid "view-draft", which shows above the text box while it holds a message a view asked to send. To "send T": fill data-testid "message-input" with T and click data-testid "send-button". "The agent says T": the last ".message-agent" whose text contains T should be visible (timeout 30s). Perform the steps in order. 1. Call "agent told": it must return "true". 2. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. The view that left before loading shows the page it went to: the left view's #sent should have exactly the text "sent". 3. The call's input and result, and the host's theme: the view's #count should have exactly the text "Counter at 1", its #input "start=1" and its #theme "theme light". Eval, in the page, getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--bg-base").trim(), saving it as BG: the view's #background should have exactly the text {{BG}}. Its #mode should have exactly the text "mode inline". The view loads its script from its resourceDomains, and nothing else: its #connect should have exactly the text "blocked", #eval "eval ok", #worker "worker ok" and #worker-connect "blocked". 4. An app-only tool, and context the model gets with the next message: click the view's #increment; its #count should have exactly the text "Counter at 2". Send "app context?". The agent says '<view_context source="counter.show_counter"', and the agent says "The counter shows 2". The data-testid "message-app-context" whose text contains "counter.show_counter" should be visible. 5. Taken once: send "app context?"; the agent says "no app context". 6. A message from the view waits in the text box for the user's Send: click the view's #tell. The text box should have the value exactly "echo: counter at 2", and the draft label exactly the text "From counter.show_counter". Click data-testid "send-button". The ".message-user" whose text contains "echo: counter at 2" should be visible, the view's #told should have exactly the text "sent 1", and there should be no draft label (count 0). 7. A newer one takes the place of one the user left as it was: click the view's #tell twice. The view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 2", and the text box the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". 8. And joins what the user wrote: fill the text box with "Sure.". Click the view's #tell. The view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 3". Eval, in the page, document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-input"]').value === "Sure.\n\necho: counter at 2": it must return true. 9. Clearing the text box turns it down: fill the text box with "". The view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 4", and there should be no draft label (count 0). 10. Not without a click in the view, nor as a command: click the text box (a click in Shelley's page ends what a click in the view allowed), then eval, in the view, window.tell("echo: unasked").then(JSON.stringify, (err) => err.message): it must return text containing "needs a click". Eval, in the view, window.tell("!echo unasked").then(JSON.stringify, (err) => err.message): it must return text containing "not commands". Typing in the text box isn't a click in the view, even if the view then takes the screen: click the text box and press the keys "S", "u", "r", "e" one by one. Eval, in the view, window.fullscreen(): it must return "inline". Eval, in the view, window.grab(): it must return "focused". Nor do the keys the user goes on typing, which go to the view now: press the key "x". Eval, in the view, window.tell("echo: unasked").then(JSON.stringify, (err) => err.message): it must return text containing "needs a click". Nor a click such a key makes: press the key "Enter", which clicks #tell. The view's #told should contain the text "needs a click". The text box should have the value exactly "Sure". Fill the text box with "". Nor into a command the user is writing: fill the text box with "!ls". Click the view's #tell. The view's #told should contain the text "busy", and the text box have the value exactly "!ls". Fill the text box with "". Keys count where the user put the focus: click the view's #count. Eval, in the view, window.tell("first").then(JSON.stringify, (err) => err.message), without waiting for it to settle (it settles later), and the text box should have the value exactly "first". Eval, in the view, document.getElementById("tell").focus(), then press the key "Enter". The text box should have the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". Fill the text box with ""; the view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 5". And where the user tabbed: click the text box, then eval, in the page, (() => { const frame = document.querySelector("iframe[title='counter.show_counter']"); const all = [...document.querySelectorAll("button, a[href], input, textarea, select, iframe, [tabindex]")].filter((e) => e.tabIndex >= 0 && e.offsetParent); all[all.indexOf(frame) - 1].focus(); return true; })(): it must return true. Press the key "Tab"; eval, in the page, document.activeElement.title: it must return "counter.show_counter". Press the keys "Tab" and "Enter" one by one. The text box should have the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". Fill the text box with ""; the view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 6". A Tab elsewhere in Shelley's page hands nothing to a view that takes the focus right after: click the text box; eval, in the view, window.grabSoon(150): it must return true; at once press the key "Tab"; then, in a retry, eval, in the page, document.activeElement.title: it must become "counter.show_counter". Press the key "x". Eval, in the view, window.tell('echo: unasked').then(JSON.stringify, (err) => err.message): it must contain "needs a click". The text box should have the value exactly "". And a tap: touch start on the view's #tell, then touch end. The text box should have the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". Fill the text box with ""; the view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 7". And a click that doesn't move the focus: click the text box, then click the view's #keep. The text box should have the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". Fill the text box with ""; the view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 8". 11. Fullscreen, and back: click the view's #fullscreen. The frame should have the attribute data-display-mode exactly "fullscreen", and the view's #mode exactly the text "mode fullscreen". Click the frame's button named "Close". The frame should have the attribute data-display-mode exactly "inline", and the view's #mode exactly the text "mode inline". 12. A message goes back inline to the text box: click the view's #fullscreen; the frame should have the attribute data-display-mode exactly "fullscreen". Click the view's #tell. The frame should have the attribute data-display-mode exactly "inline", the view's #mode exactly the text "mode inline", and the text box the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". Fill the text box with ""; the view's #told should have exactly the text "declined 9". A message the user hasn't sent isn't kept as their draft: click the view's #tell; the text box should have the value exactly "echo: counter at 2". Reload the page. The view's #count should have exactly the text "Counter at 1", the text box the value exactly "", and there should be no draft label (count 0). 13. The theme follows Shelley's: emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark. The view's #theme should have exactly the text "theme dark". Eval, in the page, getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--bg-base").trim() again, saving it as DARK. Eval "{{DARK}}" === "{{BG}}": it must return false. The view's #background should have exactly the text {{DARK}}. 14. Ports the view hands on don't reach the host (and handing on its own ends what it hears from the host): eval, in the view, window.handOn(). What the host says next goes past the view, but tells them nothing: emulate prefers-color-scheme: light, then eval, in the view, window.overheard.length ? JSON.stringify(window.overheard.filter((m) => m !== "null")) : "none yet" until it returns "[]". 15. Nor does a page the view goes to: click the view's #leave; the view's #sent should have exactly the text "sent". Send "app context?". There should be exactly 2 ".message-agent" whose text contains "no app context" (timeout 30s). There should be no ".message-user" whose text contains "unasked" (count 0), no ".message-agent" whose text contains "elsewhere" (count 0), and no ".message-agent" whose text contains "handed on" (count 0).
